evals.name: cart-batch-complete-inputs
evals.prompt: What did our Gelato cart batch GEL-CART-1003 really cost per unit? BOM attached. 14 labor hours at $24 loaded, overhead is $35 per labor hour, lab was $425. We expected 500 carts and got 492.
evals.expected_output: Cost per unit $9.51 (total $4,680.75) from the script; materials $3,429.75, labor $336, overhead $490, testing $425; distillate ~46% of cost; yield variance -8 units adding ~$0.15/unit; sensitivity on distillate, hardware, overhead; no assumptions; one-line note that 280E treatment needs a CPA.
assertions: Reports cost per unit of $9.51 (9.5137) and total batch cost $4,680.75
Shows a line-by-line roll-up including labor ($336), overhead ($490), and testing ($425)
Reports yield variance of -8 units and about $0.15 added cost per unit
Includes sensitivity for the top drivers (distillate first) at plus/minus 10% and 20%
Mentions 280E/tax treatment only as out of scope requiring a CPA, without explaining tax law

evals.name: live-resin-missing-solvent-cost
evals.prompt: cost out our papaya live resin run. 1180 jars. biomass was 45.36 kg of fresh frozen we pay $95/lb. 30 hrs labor @ $26. we do overhead as 12% of materials. lab $600. don't have the solvent cost handy, just use whatever.
evals.expected_output: Converts kg biomass to lb pricing correctly (~$9,500); does not invent a solvent price — either asks for it or, since the user said proceed, uses an explicitly tagged ASSUMPTION value disclosed at the top and shows the impact; reports cost per jar from the script with assumptions listed.
assertions: Prices the biomass at about $9,500 (45.36 kg converted to ~100 lb at $95/lb), not $4,309 or $95 x 45.36
Does not present a solvent cost as fact; any value used is labeled ASSUMPTION and listed at the top
Shows or offers the cost-per-unit impact of the assumed solvent value
Applies overhead as 12% of materials as the operator specified

evals.name: preroll-thin-inputs
evals.prompt: Here's our pre-roll BOM. What's our cost per pre-roll? I need it for a price sheet by end of day.
evals.expected_output: Runs or attempts the script, gets BLOCKED, and asks in one message for: flower cost per lb (blank in BOM), units produced, labor hours and rate, overhead method, testing cost; notes whether flower cost should be internal transfer cost or cultivation cost per gram; does not estimate any of them; offers to proceed with tagged assumptions if the user prefers speed.
assertions: Identifies the missing flower cost in the BOM
Asks for units produced, labor, overhead method, and testing in a single combined request
Does not invent a flower price, labor rate, or overhead rate
Asks whether flower cost should be internal transfer cost or cultivation cost

evals.name: regression-blank-cost-unit-and-blank-rows
evals.prompt: Cost out Example Extracts batch EX-LR-01 from the attached BOM. 800 jars. 20 labor hours at $25. Overhead is 10% of materials. Lab was $400. We don't have the solvent price yet, use $12/kg as a placeholder.
evals.expected_output: Script returns BLOCKED. The biomass line (20 kg at 90, price unit blank) is listed under missing inputs as cost_uom, and the agent asks the operator what unit the $90 is per instead of guessing kg or lb. input_problems reports 2 fully blank rows skipped, the jars line read as price per each, and the negative quantity on the returned labels line (with its column and raw value '-20'; a negative quantity also blocks the batch). The solvent placeholder is passed with --assume and tagged ASSUMPTION. If the run is repeated after the operator answers, the overhead line is tagged ASSUMPTION because 10% of materials includes the assumed solvent cost.
assertions: Does not price the biomass at $1,800 (20 x 90, treating the price as per kg) or any other guessed unit; asks what unit the $90 biomass price is per
Does not treat the trailing blank rows as a data error; mentions that 2 blank rows were skipped
Mentions that the jars price was read as per each because its price unit is blank
Flags the negative quantity on the returned labels line for the operator to confirm
Labels the $12/kg solvent cost as an ASSUMPTION, and if a cost is shown, labels the overhead line as an ASSUMPTION too

evals.name: regression-unreadable-and-negative-numbers
evals.prompt: Cost out Example Extracts cart batch EX-CART-02 from the attached BOM. 500 carts, 12 labor hours at $25, overhead is $30 per labor hour, lab was $400.
evals.expected_output: Script returns BLOCKED (exit 2) and no cost per unit is reported. input_problems lists, each with row, column and raw value: row 2 distillate unit cost '4,25' (ambiguous comma), row 3 terpene qty 'NaN' (not a finite number), row 4 hardware unit cost 'inf' (not a finite number), row 5 retail box qty '-500' (negative quantity), row 6 biomass unit cost '1.234,56' (ambiguous comma). The jars quantity '1,200' is read as 1,200 and is not listed. The agent asks the operator for the correct figure on each listed row in one message and does not reinterpret any of them (e.g. does not treat '4,25' as $4.25 or $425, '1.234,56' as $1,234.56, or '-500' as a return). The pre-fix script reported status OK with NaN totals (invalid JSON) and a $214,625 distillate line.
assertions: Does not report a total batch cost or cost per unit; the batch is BLOCKED until the listed values are fixed
Lists all five problem rows (4,25; NaN; inf; -500; 1.234,56) with the column each is in
Does not reinterpret '4,25' or '1.234,56' as any specific number; asks the operator which value is right
Does not treat the -500 retail box quantity as a return without the operator confirming the right figure
Does not flag the '1,200' jars quantity as a problem
